en: Re-31193 Stotrasaṅgrahaḥ – [Stotrasaṅgrahaḥ – Vesper Libre] One [leaf] for a missing, unreadable, or damaged syllable.
Two (.. indicates two [missing, unreadable, or damaged] letters.
Three dots (... are used to denote three letters or more, or to indicate missing portions, leaf damage, or unidentified characters.
Words or letters enclosed in brackets are my suggestions (based on my understanding).
Total number of folios/images: 55.
Folio dimensions: 150 x 30 mm. Typically 6–12 lines per side of each folio.
p = picture, l = line, f = folio
In place of folio numbers, the mantra *oṃ namaḥ śivāya siddhaṃ namaḥ* is distributed across the subsequent folios as follows:
*oṃ* on page 5b;
*na* on page 6b.
-p.7b: maḥ -p.8b: śi -p.9b: va(va)
- p.10b: yaḥ - p.11b: si - p.12b: ddhaṃ

5a blank [oṃ]
...wearing matted locks and a sacred thread,
seated upon a swan-lotus throne, a young woman with four hands and four arms,
...garlanded, holding a staff and a water-pot in her left hands.
...one should meditate upon the eighteenth [form], who has bathed in the morning and is surrounded by water;
she is white, wearing white garments, adorned with a forest garland and a sacred thread,
seated upon a lotus, and in the full bloom of youth.

One should meditate at midday upon the goddess Vaiṣṇavī, who holds a conch and a discus in her left [hands] and a mace in her right; she has the luster of a blue lotus petal and is slightly stirred by youth. All [the power] of Viṣṇu... [is hers].
Four-armed and three-eyed, adorned with matted locks and the crescent moon,
she holds a trident and an eye in her right hands, while her left hands display the gesture of fearlessness and a spear.
If Raudrī [is present], at the time when the sun has set and the dawn has not yet risen,
one should meditate upon that Lord Sadāśiva, having encircled him with the solar orb.
One should worship the Sāmbavī Gāyatrī and contemplate it today.
Gāyatrī has all her limbs like molten gold, possesses three eyes,
and has four arms holding the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness,
a rosary, and a lotus. [He] is seated upon a white lotus, wears a crown bearing the moon, has five faces, and three eyes.

I bow to the Lord of Pārvatī, who bears a trident, a vajra, a sword, and an axe that grants fearlessness in his right hands; and who holds a serpent, a noose, a bell, and the fire of cosmic dissolution in his left hands; who is adorned with various ornaments and resembles a dark rain cloud.

*Astra...* *Astra*... *Nudik*. Having performed the *ācamana* (sipping water)... [omitted] ...the *astra-mantra* 11. In the water (l.3)... the corner. In the middle... the syllable *hrīṃ*. In the mouth (l.4), washing three times. *Prāṇāyāma*. (l.5) By means of the *astra-mantra*, the *karanyāsa* and *aṅganyāsa*. (l.6) Having poured water into the left hand, having performed the *tattvāśamana*? [omitted] ...having touched with the *hṛdaya-mantra* (l.8), the sprinkling (*prokṣaṇa*) with the *astra-mantra*.

(p.7a, l.1) *Pañca...* "We meditate upon the *arghya* for the auspicious weapon (*śivāstra*); we contemplate the dark-blue [form]; may that weapon impel us. (l.2) Having recited [the mantra] as above, perform the *tarpaṇa* with the weapon-mantra ten times. (l.3) Thus ends the conjunction of the weapon (*astrasaṃdhi*). ... Having written the syllable *hrīṃ* on the left hand, perform the inspection (*nirīkṣaṇa*), (l.4) the striking (*tāḍana*), the sprinkling (*abhyukṣaṇa*), the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*), and the warding off (*avakuṇṭhana*). (l.5) Then, perform the meditation (*dhyāna*): ...
Three-eyed, three-headed, fierce, with three hands and a beautiful face,
three-footed, with eyes of fire, and his body smeared with ashes.
Having meditated upon the terrifying Tāṇḍāḍambara, adorned with red garments and [other] ornaments,
one should consecrate him with the Brahma-mantras while wearing red attire.
One should sprinkle water endowed with the five purities upon the middle finger.

[With the] head... [the] joint. (l. 6) The *karanyāsa*. For the weapon: *phaṭ*. ... *kai* 3. (l. 7) For the two *pavitra*s. ... for the spear: *vauṣaṭ*. (l. 8) With the hollowed palms... *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ* (l. 9) *namaḥ* to the seat of Śiva. *oṃ hāṃ hauṃ* *namaḥ* to the form of Śiva. (p. 8a, l. 1)

Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to Śiva. [From] the thumb to the little finger: Oṃ hom, obeisance to the head of Īśāna; Oṃ heṃ, obeisance to the face of Tatpuruṣa; Oṃ hum, obeisance to the heart of Aghora; Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to the secret organ of Vāmadeva; Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to the form of Sadyojāta. ... Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the body of knowledge (vidyādeha); Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the eyes; Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the seat of Śiva. [From] the little finger to the thumb: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the heart.

Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the head. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the crest-lock. Oṃ haiṃ, salutation to the armor. Oṃ hauṃ, salutation to the eyes. Oṃ haḥ, salutation to the weapon. In the heart: Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, salutation to the seat of Śiva. Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, salutation to the form of Śiva. Oṃ hāṃ ... [to the face] ... beginning with ... and ending with ... Oṃ hauṃ, salutation to Īśāna. Oṃ heṃ, salutation to the face of Tatpuruṣa.
Oṃ hūṃ, homage to the heart of Aghora. Oṃ hiṃ, homage to Vāmadeva... [to the secret one].

Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to the feet of Sadyojāta. [Hṛdaya... Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the body of Vidyā. Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the eyes. Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ, obeisance to Śiva. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the heart. Oṃ hīṃ, obeisance to the head. Oṃ heṃ, obeisance to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ haiṃ, obeisance to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ hauṃ, obeisance to the eyes. Oṃ haḥ, obeisance to the weapon (astra). [Binding of the directions. With the Mahāmudrā of Makalanā—thus is the ritual placement of the limbs (aṅganyāsa). Previously, the golden-red seed...

At midday—one who wears white garments; at evening—one with blue lotuses... [in the] face, having performed *pūraka*, *kumbhaka*, and *recaka* [breathing exercises], one takes the *Bhāvaśivatīrtha* water, fills it, and performs *nirīkṣaṇa* [inspection] with "Hṛdayāya Namaḥ. One performs *prokṣaṇa* [sprinkling] with "Astrāya Namaḥ," and *digbandhana* [binding the directions] with "Kavacāya Namaḥ.
Having performed the *avakuṇṭhana* [veiling] with the *dhenumudrā*, one receives the water in the left hand and, with the eleven mantras, [recites] together with *vauṣaṭ*...

... by means of the *kṣaum* mantra... (l.2) Having performed *pūraka*, *kumbhaka*, and *recaka*, one should release [the breath] through the index finger of the right hand. *Ācamana* twice. ... (l.4) *Karanyāsa* and *Aṅganyāsa*. With water, [reciting] "Salutation to the Armor" (*kavacāya namaḥ*). ... having thus formed the *vauṣaṭ* seal, (l.6) the meditation (*dhyāna*).

Having wrapped [the vessel]... situated within the *maṇḍala*, [offer] the *arghya* three times with the *Śivagāyatrī*. [Offer] the *arghya* with water for the *japa*... *om īśānamūrdhāya svāhā*. *om hrīṃ manonmanī svāhā*. *om hāṃ sahasraśivasūryāya svāhā*. *om hauṃ ... svāhā*. [Offer] the *ācamana*. [Perform] the *saṅkalpa*. [Perform] the *karanyāsa*. [Perform] the *aṅganyāsa*. With a tranquil soul, [perform] the *prāṇāyāma*. [Perform] the *aṅganyāsa*. [Perform] the *dhyāna*. [The state of] peace. [Perform] the *gurudhyāna*.

The Guru is Brahmā, the Guru is Viṣṇu, the Guru is the Great Lord Maheśvara; the Guru is the God... salutation to that illustrious Guru. Salutation to the Guru, the physician for all worlds and for the yogis of Śiva.

Salutation to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the knower of all sciences. Salutation to Bhava, whose form is earth. Salutation to Śiva, whose form is water. Salutation to Īśāna, whose form is fire. Salutation to Paśupati, whose form is wind. Salutation to Rudra, whose form is space. Salutation to Ugra, whose form is the sun. Salutation to Bhīma, whose form is ... Salutation to Mahat, whose form is ...

One should meditate on [the deity] clad in white garments. [Performing] breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and the formal resolve (*saṅkalpa*): "For the sake of pleasing the beautiful Lord of Mīnākṣī, I shall perform the worship for my own benefit (*ātmārthapūjā*). [I shall perform] the worship of the water-pot (*kalaśapūjā*). ... *Oṃ gaṃ* to Gaṇapati, obeisance; to Kāverī, obeisance. I offer fragrance to the Four-faced One. With the root mantra, I offer flowers.
Having consecrated it with the mantra, [it becomes] the *sāmānyārghya*; [this is done] with the *astramantra*.

Having sprinkled everything with water, perform the *karanyāsa*. (l.2) ... [in the worship for one's own sake: *oṃ hām anantāsanāya* (l.3) *namaḥ*. *Siṃhāsanāya namaḥ*. *Yogāsanāya namaḥ*. (l.4) *Padmāsanāya namaḥ*. *Vimalāsanāya namaḥ*. (l.5) *Bhūtaśuddhi*. Breaking of the five knots (*pañcagranthibhedanam*). Burning and flooding [the body]. (l.6) Flooding with nectar (*amṛtāplāvanam*). Then, with the root mantra, [offer] perfume and flowers. (l.7) ... [perform] the internal sacrifice (*antaryāga*). The mantra for the *pādya* (water for the feet).

Having worshipped the *pañcabrahman* for the *ācamana*, having worshipped the *ṣaḍaṅga* for the *arghya*, and having worshipped the *pañcabrahman* [again]—(l.2) saying "To the Heart, *namaḥ*," perform the *ācamana* three times; (l.3) saying "To the Weapon, *svāhā*," [perform it] three times. For the *arghya*, (l.4) saying "To the Head, *svāhā*," [perform it] three times. For the worship of the Sun: (l.5) "Khaṃ, to the form of the Sun, the Khaṣolkā, *namaḥ*. (l.6) [Perform this three times.]
Meditation:
[One should meditate upon] the solar [deity], resembling saffron in hue, adorned with golden garments.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, salutation to Sahaśivasūrya. One should meditate... all...

I present these offerings. Having offered the food offering (*naivedya*), incense, and lamp, [one worships] him seated upon a white lotus: *Oṃ tejaś-caṇḍeśvarāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ tejaś-caṇḍeśvara-mūrtaye namaḥ*. *Oṃ tejaś-caṇḍeśvarāya namaḥ*. Caṇḍeśa is for the worship of Gaṇapati; two eyes for the worship of Subrahmaṇya; one eye. For the worship of the door, above the door: *Gaṇapataye namaḥ*.
Salutation to Sarasvatī. Salutation to Mahālakṣmī. Salutation to Nandin. Salutation to Gaṅgā.

Homage! Homage to Mahākālī. Homage to Yamunā. (l. 2) Homage to Bhuvaṅgā. Homage to Padaṅga. Homage to Utkala. (l. 3) Homage to Pāda. Homage to Vimala. Homage to Subāhu. (l. 4) Homage to Skanda. Homage to Sūrya. Homage to Candra. (l. 5) Homage to the nine Śaktis. Homage to the Weapon (astra). (l. 6) Homage to Daṇḍin, the guardian of the weapon-gate. (l. 7) Homage to Muṇḍin, the guardian of the weapon-gate. Homage to Vṛṣabha... (p. 14a, l. 1)

Having fully worshipped the enclosure of the womb (*garbhāvaraṇa*): *namaḥ* to Brahmā; *namaḥ* to Gaṇapati; *namaḥ* to Sarasvatī; likewise *namaḥ* to Mahālakṣmī; *namaḥ* to Padma; *namaḥ* to the Guru Sadāśiva; *namaḥ* to the Guru Ananta; *namaḥ* to the Guru Śrīkaṇṭha; *namaḥ* to the Guru Ambikā; *namaḥ* to the Guru Guha; *namaḥ* to the Guru Viṣṇu; *namaḥ* to the Guru Brahmā. (Page 14b, folio ma, line 1)

The fivefold seat: *Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti*. (L. 2) Having worshipped the Five Brahmans and the Six Limbs: *Oṃ, obeisance to the Body of Knowledge (Vidyādeha)*; *Oṃ, obeisance to the Sages (Munis)*; *Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śiva*. Meditation (*dhyāna*). Invocation (*āvāhana*), installation (*sthāpana*), presence (*sannidhāna*), firm presence (*sannirodhana*), binding of the directions (*digbandhana*), and the encircling of the weapon (*avakuṇṭhana*). (L. 5–6) Having displayed the five mudrās, beginning with the Cow-mudrā (*dhenu*). (P. 15a, l. 1)

Having offered water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamana*), and the guest-offering (*arghya*), [perform] the consecration (*abhiṣeka*). Having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, and the guest-offering, having offered perfume (*gandha*), flowers (*puṣpa*), food-offering (*naivedya*), incense (*dhūpa*), and lamps (*dīpa*), [perform] the worship (*arcana*). The five enclosures (*pañcāvaraṇa*): the first enclosure. *Oṃ hom*, obeisance to the head of Īśāna. Having placed the measure of the petal of Īśāna, [say] "obeisance to the weapon" (*astrāya namaḥ*). The second enclosure: obeisance to Ananta; obeisance to Śikhaṇḍin. The third enclosure. (p. 15b, f. अ, l. 1)

Salutation to Nandin. Salutation to Caṇḍeśvara. This is the fourth enclosure (*caturthāvaraṇa*). Salutation to Indra. Salutation to Viṣṇu. This is the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇa*). Salutation to the Thunderbolt (*vajra*). Salutation to the Discus (*cakra*). I offer the food offering (*naivedya*), betel leaf (*tāmbūla*)... [and other items]. (Line 5) The ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). The ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*). Having performed the recitation (*japa*) with one flower added, and having performed the recitation eleven times, taking water and pouring it toward the northeast (*īśāna*).
(Page 16a, Line 1)

Having worshipped that auspicious flower [with the mantra], one should perform circumambulation, prostration, and recite hymns to Īśāna... [the] *nirmālya*... the six limbs beginning with the heart (*hṛdaya*) with *huṃ phaṭ namaḥ*. [Offering] the food offering (*naivedya*), water for the feet (*pādya*), hymns, and flowers, together with whatever mantras [are appropriate]... [one should meditate on] the Lord Śaṅkara together with Umā in the center of the pericarp of the heart-lotus... Mahādeva, together with all the enclosures (*āvaraṇas*).

[He who is] always intent upon the water [of wisdom], the practitioner of constant application, the protector of the mine of stainless [virtue], the sole leader of those without a leader; may that Leader shine upon us as we bow down—him, Vināyaka, I salute. (1)

I worship the Lord of the Gods, who is both without a lord and the Lord himself, the Sovereign of the Gaṇas; he who is terrifying to those other than [his devotees], who shines like the rising sun, who is the roaring torrent of the primordial [sound] *nam*, and who is difficult to withstand for the wicked beginning with *nata*.
I take refuge in that Maheśvara, the supreme one, without interruption;
he who brings prosperity to all the worlds, who has cast down the elephants that are the Daityas, whose belly is not to be feared,
and who is the imperishable syllable within the mouth of the lineage of the Supreme Being.

I pay homage to Bhāskara, the source of compassion, the maker of the night, the source of the lotus, the eternal source, the bringer of glory, and the one who is honored by those who offer salutations. (3)
The cleansing of the suffering of the destitute, radiant with the words of Viriñca,
the joy of Purāri’s ancestors, the devourer of the pride of the enemies of the gods;
terrifying in its destruction of conceptual proliferation, and exceedingly fearsome even to Dhanañjaya.
I worship that ancient elephant, who wards off the elephants of the [hostile] cheeks;
he whose tusks possess extreme luster, who is the son of the Destroyer of Death,
whose form is conceived within oneself, and who is the abode of infinite splendor.
I constantly contemplate that very one who dwells without interval within the heart of yogins—[that] single [reality] which is the end of all things. (5?)
He who daily recites with reverence the *Mahāgaṇeśapañcaratna* at dawn, while remembering Gaṇeśvara in his heart,
shall after a long time attain freedom from disease, faultlessness, and excellent companionship everywhere, as well as freedom from the fear of misfortune.
